detail.body:
**Closed after an applicability review.** The measured ~16% reduction applies to a constructed linked-record workload with explicit successor IDs and synthetic tool delays. It does not establish a general rollout or end-to-end RL training speedup. The current implementation has not demonstrated value on a representative real RL workload, so this draft is being withdrawn. The implementation and recorded test results are retained for reference.

---

### What does this PR do?

A linked-record tool often returns the exact identifier the model will request next. This PR adds an opt-in `ReadAhead` helper that starts that one immutable read during the next model turn and delivers it only when the model actually requests the matching key. A runnable `ToolAgentLoop` example scopes the reader to a trajectory and cleans up pending HTTP work on completion, failure, or cancellation.

This is a separate direction from #8136's continuation admission burst. That PR is now closed and did not establish an isolated scheduling benefit. This contribution overlaps tool waiting with model work; it does not modify the model, inference kernels, backend scheduling, or default agent loop behavior.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [tool prefetch](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+tool+prefetch+in%3Atitle), [read-ahead](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22read-ahead%22), [speculative tool](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22speculative+tool%22+in%3Atitle), [references to #8136](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8136+in%3Abody). No open PR implementing this tool-read overlap was found. Broad search hits in checkpoint handling are unrelated. There is no originating issue to close.
- [x] Use the required module/type title format.

### Test

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tools/test_read_ahead_on_cpu.py \
  tests/tools/test_function_tool_on_cpu.py \
  tests/tools/test_mixed_tools_on_cpu.py \
  tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_call_tool_on_cpu.py -q
# 61 passed; one existing Ray deprecation warning.

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never
# All 14 hooks passed. Staged hooks also passed after adding the documentation index entry.

git diff --cached --check
# Passed.
```

Six helper cases cover one-step overlap without recursive reads, wrong-key fallback, speculative-failure retry, demanded-failure propagation, and cancellation of both unused and consumed prefetches. Five added example cases use real local HTTP and the existing tool dispatch: concurrent trajectory isolation with read-ahead off/on, and cleanup on normal return, model error, and cancellation. Model turns in these CPU integration cases are scripted; they are not model evaluations. Existing `*_on_cpu.py` discovery includes these tests. The new RST page also parses without warnings.

**Current-commit real-model HTTP E2E:** commit `bde9bde4864ba15c3fd942ce280fb7bc628fc2fb`, full MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL revision `5711b268169967567844e1e560e8a3966da959b1`, eight MI355X GPUs. The committed `ReadAheadAgentLoop` and `ReadRecordTool` were loaded through Hydra and the standard tool registry, using their committed YAML files. The harness uses the real `LLMServerClient` and default Ray load balancer; a Ray adapter forwards actual prompt token IDs to the model server and consumes live SSE output. Record reads go through a real aiohttp service with synthetic immutable linked-record delays of 0.25/0.5/1/2 seconds.

The same server ran **one off → on → off cycle**. Each phase had a four-task smoke, three stable warmups, and three formal 64-trajectory batches: nine formal batches total. Native FCFS, async scheduling disabled, sparse4096 graph settings, model and workload stayed fixed. Each batch used a fresh prefix-cache salt. Model loading and warmup were excluded. The old scheduling PR was not enabled.

| Mode | Three batch completion times (s) | Mean ± sample SD (s) |
|---|---|---|
| Off, before | 31.811044 / 31.616662 / 31.635930 | 31.687879 ± 0.107099 |
| On | 26.452443 / 26.420624 / 26.787237 | 26.553435 ± 0.203103 |
| Off, recheck | 31.579407 / 31.315902 / 31.611394 | 31.502234 ± 0.162159 |

Completion time fell by **16.20% / 15.71%** relative to the two baselines; baseline drift was -0.59%. The last-finishing trajectory's exposed read wait averaged 24.556 → 19.039 → 24.561 seconds, with about 5.510 seconds of overlapping reads when enabled. Its physical reads still took about 24.52 seconds; model service request time averaged 6.498 → 6.960 → 6.497 seconds. The gain comes from overlapping tool waiting and model generation.

**576/576 formal trajectories passed** independent checks of ordered record IDs, full returned values, calculator inputs, and final answers. Every batch made 624 model requests, 496 physical HTTP reads, and 64 calculator calls. Enabled batches reused 432 prefetches, without extra reads. All physical requests retained their injected delays, no unconsumed dependency was crossed, and HTTP tasks, helper tasks, Ray counters, and backend queues were drained. Request and token counts reconcile with server metrics.

| Mode | Generated tokens in the three formal batches |
|---|---|
| Off, before | 18702 / 18536 / 18626 |
| On | 18917 / 18728 / 18862 |
| Off, recheck | 18732 / 18844 / 18748 |

Three further live-model diagnostics passed: turn-limit termination, an injected model transport failure after the first live turn, and caller cancellation. Each canceled the deliberately blocked successor HTTP request and left no pending work. These are separate from the timed batches. Scripted preflight results are also excluded from model-quality and performance results.

Executed commands in the prepared AAC container (environment, launch commands, source and protocol hashes are retained with the results):

```bash
bash "$AAC_TASK_DIR/protocol/continue_one_cycle.sh"
"$AAC_PYTHON" "$AAC_TASK_DIR/protocol/audit_e2e.py" "$AAC_JOB_DIR"
# One cycle and all three diagnostics passed; controller exit code 0.
```

The downloaded raw results were audited again locally with the UV-managed environment; they produced an identical aggregate. All 1,277 frozen source/protocol manifest entries passed checksum verification. No serving-cache writes were observed during timed regions; file timestamps are a proxy, not a full compilation trace. The independent auditor rejected five deliberately corrupted traces covering dependency order, shortened delays, extra reads, wrong values, and pending work.

This validates the current PR HTTP example against a live full model. It is still a deterministic linked-record workload with synthetic service delays and no shared tool-capacity limit. No RL optimizer or weight updates ran, and output tokens were not identical. Three samples per state in one cycle do not establish a general RL or production remote-service speedup.

Operational record: the test was reduced to one cycle during model loading by handing control to a replacement controller in the same container. The original wrapper remained paused; after the replacement exited 0 and the model-stop GPU report showed zero use/memory and no KFD processes, allocation 48534 was intentionally canceled to release it. The parked wrapper’s later GPU-report hook logged a ROCm shared-memory error; the successful pre-cancellation model-stop report and the later error are both preserved. No second or third comparison cycle ran.

The raw results and frozen harness/source archive are retained by the contributor, outside the PR: `job-48534-results.tar.gz`, SHA256 `b3ec030a231b09e6e295a3dc9db8c9570662efb52f2c19f1e9eeffd9fd14eecb`. This fresh E2E result supersedes the earlier dedicated-helper experiment as evidence for the PR implementation; the documentation labels the earlier measurement as historical.

### API and Usage Example

```python
from verl.tools.read_ahead import ReadAhead

reader = ReadAhead(fetch_record, lambda record: record.get("next_record_id"))
try:
    # Call read only when the model requests the key; keep reader across turns.
    result = await reader.read(record_id)
finally:
    await reader.aclose()  # At trajectory end, after demanded reads stop.
```

The example agent/tool YAML files are under `examples/tutorial/agent_loop_get_started/`. Configure an immutable record snapshot URL and select the custom loop, then set its `read_ahead` option to `true` (default `false`). `docs/advance/tool_read_ahead.rst` gives the service contract and rollout overrides.

### Design & Code Changes

- Keep at most one speculative result per trajectory. Derive the next key only from the consumed result; never recursively follow an unconsumed record.
- Reuse only a matching key. Cancel and join mismatches; retry failed speculation on demand; propagate demanded errors.
- Require serial reads, complete operation keys, immutable/read-only data, and cancellation-aware async fetches. The example serializes reads and binds its reader with a per-run context, without storing tasks in serialized outputs.
- Keep cleanup at trajectory scope because ordinary `BaseTool.release` runs after each call. Close the reader before its HTTP session.
- Add documentation, tests, and the 2026 individual-contributor header to the existing license allow-list for the new files.

Related work: [Conveyor](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00059v2), [PASTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18897v3), and [LLMCompiler](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04511v3). This is deterministic one-step lookahead, not a reproduction of learned prediction or joint scheduling. Wrong predictions can waste reads; service-wide admission limits remain the caller's responsibility, and cancelling an HTTP request does not guarantee remote work stops.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide and agent instructions.
- [x] Install pre-commit and run all repository hooks.
- [x] Add documentation and usage example.
- [x] Add tests covered by the existing CPU workflow.
- [ ] Human submitter review of every changed line and independent execution of the relevant tests before requesting review.
- [ ] Request project CI when the draft is ready.

No recipe submodule change is involved.

### AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with research, implementation, tests, the prior experiment, current-commit HTTP E2E validation, and PR preparation. The commit includes attribution trailers. This is a draft for the human submitter's review; it does not attest that the human has reviewed the new lines or independently rerun the tests.

@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@
+Tool read-ahead
+===============
+
+Last updated: 10/12/2026.
+
+When a tool returns the identifier of the next record, an agent can start reading
+that record while the model generates its next turn. ``verl.tools.read_ahead.ReadAhead``
+provides this opt-in overlap for immutable, read-only data. The model still chooses
+the next call: the prepared result is delivered only when its requested key matches.
+This does not change model inference or the backend request scheduler.
+
+Use it for snapshot pagination or linked records whose next identifier is available
+in the previous result. It is unsuitable for writes, mutable data, or a next query
+that depends on reasoning the model has not performed yet. Even a read-only API can
+have billing, rate limits, or server load: speculative reads must be acceptable to
+the tool owner.
+
+Using the helper
+----------------
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+   from verl.tools.read_ahead import ReadAhead
+
+   reader = ReadAhead(fetch_record, lambda record: record.get("next_record_id"))
+   try:
+       # Call this only after the model actually requests this record.
+       result = await reader.read(record_id)
+       # Deliver result to the model; one successor may now be read concurrently.
+   finally:
+       # Close at trajectory end, after all demanded reads have stopped.
+       await reader.aclose()
+
+Keep the reader alive across model turns, with one reader per trajectory. Calls to
+``read`` must be serial. The key must identify the entire operation, including any
+arguments, authorization scope, or snapshot affecting its result. ``fetch`` must be
+an async coroutine that supports cancellation, and ``successor`` must be a pure
+callback using only the result just returned to the caller.
+
+There is at most one pending result. A completed prefetch does not recursively read
+its successor until the model consumes it. A different requested key cancels and
+joins the unused task before fetching the actual key. A speculative failure retries
+the demanded read; a demanded failure propagates. ``aclose`` retrieves unused errors
+and cancels unused work, and is safe to call again.
+
+This bounds speculation per trajectory, not across a worker or cluster. Apply the
+tool service's capacity limits to ``fetch`` and measure wasted reads when predictions
+miss. Cancelling an HTTP client request does not guarantee the remote server stops
+work. Wrapping blocking I/O with ``asyncio.to_thread`` also does not make that I/O
+cancellable.
+
+ToolAgentLoop example
+---------------------
+
+The example at ``examples/tutorial/agent_loop_get_started/read_ahead.py`` uses
+``BaseTool`` and a custom ``ToolAgentLoop``. Each ``run`` scopes a reader and an HTTP
+session to its own context, serializes reads with a lock, and closes both in
+``finally``. This matters because the standard loop calls ``BaseTool.release`` after
+each individual tool call; ending the reader there would cancel the desired overlap.
+No tasks or sessions are stored in serialized trajectory output.
+
+The record service must expose a fixed snapshot as ``GET <records_url>/<id>.json``:
+
+.. code-block:: json
+
+   {"record_id": 123, "value": 17, "next_record_id": 456}
+
+The terminal record has ``"next_record_id": null``. Deploy the service where all
+rollout workers can reach it, and edit ``records_url`` in ``read_ahead_agent.yaml``.
+It is a snapshot URL, not a mutable "latest" endpoint. The example needs ``aiohttp``,
+which is already used by the rollout environment.
+
+Add these overrides to an existing tool-agent training configuration:
+
+.. code-block:: bash
+
+   actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.default_agent_loop=read_ahead_agent \
+   actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.agent_loop_config_path=examples/tutorial/agent_loop_get_started/read_ahead_agent.yaml \
+   actor_rollout_ref.rollout.multi_turn.tool_config_path=examples/tutorial/agent_loop_get_started/read_ahead_tools.yaml
+
+Keep the model's existing tool parser configuration. Dataset prompts should ask the
+model to follow the returned ``next_record_id`` one call at a time. The example
+starts with ``read_ahead: false``; set it to ``true`` in the agent YAML to enable
+overlap. Both modes use the same HTTP fetch and return the same record schema.
+
+Measured scope
+--------------
+
+An experiment on 2026-10-12 used the full MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL model (revision
+``5711b268169967567844e1e560e8a3966da959b1``), 8 MI355X GPUs, and the real verl
+ToolAgentLoop with 64 trajectories. Tools read immutable linked records with injected
+0.25/0.5/1/2 second delays. The same running server executed off/on/off phases, each
+with a four-task quality check, three stable warmups, and three measured batches.
+Model, prompts, native FCFS scheduling and sparse4096 graph configuration were fixed.
+Startup and warmup were excluded. vLLM version was ``0.30.1rc1.dev143+g29468dde8``.
+
+.. list-table:: Batch completion time, seconds
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Mode
+     - Three measured batches
+     - Mean ± sample standard deviation
+   * - Off, before
+     - 31.646806 / 31.437801 / 31.572598
+     - 31.552402 ± 0.105956
+   * - On
+     - 26.126972 / 26.439359 / 26.370070
+     - 26.312134 ± 0.164054
+   * - Off, recheck
+     - 31.309377 / 31.495038 / 31.507548
+     - 31.437321 ± 0.110979
+
+Completion time fell 16.6% against the first baseline and 16.3% against the recheck;
+baseline drift was -0.36%. The last trajectory's exposed read wait fell from 24.518
+to 18.914 seconds. Its physical reads still took 24.521 seconds, with 5.609 seconds
+overlapped. Its model service calls took 6.927 seconds versus 6.429 seconds before:
+the benefit was reduced exposed tool waiting, not faster model computation.
+
+All 576 trajectories passed checks of ordered record IDs, returned values,
+calculator inputs, and final answers. Each batch made 624 model requests, 496
+physical reads, and 64 calculator calls. Each enabled batch reused 432 prefetches
+without extra physical reads; no readers remained pending. Output token totals
+were 18704/18711/18920, 18596/18820/18729, and 18879/18618/18780 respectively:
+token-by-token equality is not claimed.
+
+These measurements used the helper in a dedicated linked-record harness before
+this contribution. The four helper method bodies are equivalent to the measured
+implementation; the HTTP example above is new and has CPU integration coverage,
+not a new GPU performance measurement. The original result archive is retained by
+the contributor with SHA256
+``3fc719bd956a37a6ff4ea1e55a9d7fecebacbae288d2faf849de788a45670297``.
+There were no RL optimizer or weight updates. These results do not establish a
+general RL speedup, benefits for real remote services, or an arbitrary prediction
+hit rate. The deterministic chain had no shared tool executor capacity limit.
+
+Related work
+------------
+
+- `Conveyor <https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00059v2>`_: overlap tool execution with
+  generation once required inputs are available. Here the overlap spans adjacent
+  model turns, rather than a partially generated program.
+- `PASTE <https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18897v3>`_: bounded speculative tool work and
+  matching actual calls before exposing results. This helper uses a deterministic
+  successor, without its learned predictor or joint scheduling system.
+- `LLMCompiler <https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04511v3>`_: execute independent ready
+  calls concurrently. Linked records retain their dependencies; this helper does
+  not read through unseen future results.

+"""ToolAgentLoop example for linked records served from an immutable snapshot."""
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from typing import Any
+
+import aiohttp
+
+from verl.experimental.agent_loop.agent_loop import AgentLoopOutput
+from verl.experimental.agent_loop.tool_agent_loop import ToolAgentLoop
+from verl.tools.base_tool import BaseTool
+from verl.tools.read_ahead import ReadAhead
+from verl.tools.schemas import ToolResponse
+
+_record_reader: ContextVar[tuple[ReadAhead[int, dict], asyncio.Lock]] = ContextVar("record_reader")
+
+
+class ReadRecordTool(BaseTool):
+    """Read a record using the current trajectory's reader."""
+
+    async def execute(self, instance_id: str, parameters: dict[str, Any], **kwargs):
+        """Return only the record explicitly requested by the model."""
+        record_id = parameters["record_id"]
+        if type(record_id) is not int:
+            raise ValueError("record_id must be an integer")
+        reader, lock = _record_reader.get()
+        async with lock:
+            result = await reader.read(record_id)
+        return ToolResponse(text=json.dumps(result)), 0.0, {}
+
+
+class ReadAheadAgentLoop(ToolAgentLoop):
+    """Scope HTTP reads to one trajectory, including exceptional termination."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, records_url: str, read_ahead: bool = False, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        self.records_url = records_url.rstrip("/")
+        self.read_ahead = read_ahead
+
+    async def run(self, sampling_params: dict[str, Any], priority: int = 0, **kwargs) -> AgentLoopOutput:
+        """Keep at most one successor read alive between model turns."""
+        async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=30)) as client:
+
+            async def fetch(record_id: int) -> dict:
+                async with client.get(f"{self.records_url}/{record_id}.json") as response:
+                    response.raise_for_status()
+                    return await response.json()
+
+            def successor(record: dict) -> int | None:
+                next_id = record.get("next_record_id")
+                return next_id if self.read_ahead and type(next_id) is int else None
+
+            reader = ReadAhead(fetch, successor)
+            token = _record_reader.set((reader, asyncio.Lock()))
+            try:
+                return await super().run(sampling_params, priority=priority, **kwargs)
+            finally:
+                _record_reader.reset(token)
+                await reader.aclose()

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enabled", [False, True])
+async def test_read_ahead_example_isolates_concurrent_trajectories(monkeypatch, enabled):
+    """Matching keys in two trajectories must not share speculative results."""
+    from verl.experimental.agent_loop.tool_agent_loop import ToolAgentLoop
+
+    calls = []
+    both_prefetched = asyncio.Event()
+
+    async def fetch(request):
+        record_id = int(request.match_info["record_id"])
+        calls.append(record_id)
+        if calls.count(2) == 2:
+            both_prefetched.set()
+        return web.json_response({"record_id": record_id, "next_record_id": 2 if record_id == 1 else None})
+
+    async def model_turns(loop, *args, **kwargs):
+        first = await _read_record(loop, 1)
+        if enabled:
+            await asyncio.wait_for(both_prefetched.wait(), timeout=5)
+        second = await _read_record(loop, first["next_record_id"])
+        return [first, second]
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ToolAgentLoop, "run", model_turns)
+    app = web.Application()
+    app.router.add_get("/{record_id}.json", fetch)
+    async with TestServer(app) as server:
+        loop = _make_read_ahead_loop(str(server.make_url("")).rstrip("/"), enabled)
+        outputs = await asyncio.gather(loop.run({}), loop.run({}))
+    assert outputs == [[{"record_id": 1, "next_record_id": 2}, {"record_id": 2, "next_record_id": None}]] * 2

+        else:
+            assert await task == "finished"
+        await asyncio.wait_for(cancelled.wait(), timeout=5)
+    finally:

+import asyncio
+
+import pytest
+
+from verl.tools.read_ahead import ReadAhead
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_next_read_overlaps_model_turn_without_recursive_lookahead():
+    started = asyncio.Event()
+    calls = []
+
+    async def fetch(key):
+        calls.append(key)
+        if key == 2:
+            started.set()
+        return {"key": key, "next": key + 1 if key < 3 else None}
+
+    reader = ReadAhead(fetch, lambda value: value["next"])
+    try:
+        assert await reader.read(1) == {"key": 1, "next": 2}
+        await asyncio.wait_for(started.wait(), timeout=1)
+        assert calls == [1, 2]
+        assert await reader.read(2) == {"key": 2, "next": 3}
+        assert await reader.read(3) == {"key": 3, "next": None}
+        assert calls == [1, 2, 3]
+    finally:
+        await reader.aclose()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_different_model_argument_discards_prediction():
+    started = asyncio.Event()
+    cancelled = asyncio.Event()
+
+    async def fetch(key):
+        if key == 2:
+            started.set()
+            try:
+                await asyncio.Event().wait()
+            finally:
+                cancelled.set()
+        return {"key": key, "next": 2 if key == 1 else None}
+
+    reader = ReadAhead(fetch, lambda value: value["next"])
+    try:
+        await reader.read(1)
+        await asyncio.wait_for(started.wait(), timeout=1)
+        assert await reader.read(9) == {"key": 9, "next": None}
+        assert cancelled.is_set()
+    finally:
+        await reader.aclose()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_failed_prediction_retries_the_actual_read():
+    failed = asyncio.Event()
+    attempts = 0
+
+    async def fetch(key):
+        nonlocal attempts
+        if key == 2:
+            attempts += 1
+            if attempts == 1:
+                failed.set()
+                raise OSError("temporary failure")
+        return {"key": key, "next": 2 if key == 1 else None}
+
+    reader = ReadAhead(fetch, lambda value: value["next"])
+    try:
+        await reader.read(1)
+        await asyncio.wait_for(failed.wait(), timeout=1)
+        assert await reader.read(2) == {"key": 2, "next": None}
+        assert attempts == 2
+    finally:
+        await reader.aclose()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_actual_read_failure_is_not_hidden():
+    async def fetch(key):
+        raise OSError("read failed")
+
+    reader = ReadAhead(fetch, lambda value: None)
+    try:
+        with pytest.raises(OSError, match="read failed"):
+            await reader.read(1)
+    finally:
+        await reader.aclose()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("consume", [False, True])
+async def test_cancellation_leaves_no_background_read(consume):
+    started = asyncio.Event()
+    cancelled = asyncio.Event()
+
+    async def fetch(key):
+        if key == 2:
+            started.set()
+            try:
+                await asyncio.Event().wait()
+            finally:
+                cancelled.set()
+        return {"next": 2}
+
+    reader = ReadAhead(fetch, lambda value: value["next"])
+    await reader.read(1)
+    await asyncio.wait_for(started.wait(), timeout=1)
+    if consume:
+        demand = asyncio.create_task(reader.read(2))
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        demand.cancel()
+        with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+            await demand
+    await reader.aclose()
+    await reader.aclose()
+    assert cancelled.is_set()
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="closed"):
+        await reader.read(3)

+"""Bounded, opt-in read-ahead for immutable tool data."""
+
+import asyncio
+from collections.abc import Callable, Coroutine
+from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar
+
+K = TypeVar("K")
+V = TypeVar("V")
+
+
+class ReadAhead(Generic[K, V]):
+    """Overlap one predicted read with the next model turn.
+
+    Use one instance per trajectory, with serial calls to ``read`` and a
+    read-only, immutable data source. Keys must identify the entire read,
+    including any arguments or snapshot that can affect its result.
+    ``successor`` must use only the returned value. Results become visible
+    only when ``read`` receives the matching key. ``fetch`` must support
+    cancellation; call ``aclose`` after reads stop, including on cancellation.
+
+    Args:
+        fetch: Async read of one key, safe to run before the model asks for it.
+        successor: Pure callback returning the next key, or None to stop.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        fetch: Callable[[K], Coroutine[Any, Any, V]],
+        successor: Callable[[V], K | None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self._fetch = fetch
+        self._successor = successor
+        self._key: K | None = None
+        self._pending: asyncio.Task[V] | None = None
+        self._closed = False
+
+    async def read(self, key: K) -> V:
+        """Read the requested key, then prepare at most its next successor."""
+        if self._closed:
+            raise RuntimeError("ReadAhead is closed")
+        pending = self._pending
+        if pending is not None and key == self._key:
+            self._pending = None
+            try:
+                value = await pending
+            except Exception:
+                # A failed speculative read must not replace the demanded read.
+                value = await self._fetch(key)
+        else:
+            await self._discard()
+            value = await self._fetch(key)
+        self._key = self._successor(value)
+        if self._key is not None:
+            self._pending = asyncio.create_task(self._fetch(self._key))
+        return value
+
+    async def _discard(self) -> None:
+        if self._pending is not None:
+            self._pending.cancel()
+            await asyncio.gather(self._pending, return_exceptions=True)
+            self._pending = None
+        self._key = None
+
+    async def aclose(self) -> None:
+        """Cancel unused work and retrieve any speculative exception."""
+        self._closed = True
+        await self._discard()

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits.

# Contributor License Agreement (CLA) assistant

Streamline your workflow and let CLA assistant handle the legal side of contributions to a repository for you. CLA assistant enables contributors to sign CLAs from within a pull request.

To get started, simply store your CLA as a GitHub Gist file then link it with the repository/organisation in CLA assistant. Then sit back and relax while CLA assistant:

- Comments on each opened pull request to ask the contributor to sign the CLA
- Allows contributors to sign a CLA from within a pull request
- Authenticates the signee with their GitHub account
- Updates the status of a pull request when the contributor agrees to the CLA
- Automatically asks users to re-sign the CLA for each new pull request in the event the associated Gist & CLA has changed
- Green lights merge queues without additional CLA checks as everyone needs to have signed of on the PR level already

Repository owners can review a list of users who signed the CLA for each version of it. To get started, visit [cla-assistant.io](https://cla-assistant.io).
performed_via_github_app.name: CLA Assistant
